utterances.text: Yes, that is right. And we were also assisted by Luka Gavranovic from the Croatian Information Centre in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But can you just tell us what's written or just read to us so we can get a translation on the top left-hand corner of the map? I hope it has come out on your copy. It hasn't on mine. No, I think it's even worse on yours.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it on my sketch. In the left upper corner, you said "attacks on the Croats on 24th of July, 1992, from the villages of Brisevo and Stara Rijeka," and underneath, you see the date, "at 7.00 on the 25th of July, 1992, the Serbs celebrated their bloody victory."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before this attack took place, you've told us that there were announcements on Prijedor radio before the attack on Hambarine and the like. Were any announcements made on the radio that you, the villagers of Brisevo and Stara Rijeka should surrender?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: There were no announcements for us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Any warnings through megaphones or other methods that your village was going to be attacked in this manner?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: No, there were no warnings.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, then, unless there's any other explanation that you would like Mr. Atlija to give, may that be made an exhibit as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I first ask the office of the Prosecutor, please provide us with a copy that we also can read what evidently is written on the bottom line, and there's a signature and there is a date. Unfortunately, it hasn't come out --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, it hasn't on my copy either. But I'm not sure -- because this is a photocopy of what he provided to the Croatian authorities. So it may be the best we can do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can see both the date and the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. signature in my copy, in case you'd like to have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Atlija. We'll recopy it, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, only we had the same observations as Your Honours did..

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence, S184. And for clarification, because as regards S183, it reads "tendered as evidence." Also this document was already admitted into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Atlija, how long did the soldiers remain in your village?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Most of them dispersed the next day, the evening after the attack. Some of them, and small groups, remained and kept coming throughout the days that followed the attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you were able to go back into your village, what was the level of destruction that you noticed?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: The next day, we tried to make a round of the whole village who see who survived and who was killed. 68 houses were burned down, and 68 dead bodies were lying around.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to deal with the dead bodies in a moment, a separate issue. You say 68 houses were burnt down. Was that in total destruction, as it were, or partial?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: That was a partial number, and the church was included, too. That's what I forgot to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You said there were -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: The houses were burned down to the ground, and the walls of the church were still standing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You said there were 120 houses in the village. What about other houses that hadn't been burnt down, were they damaged?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Some were, but we didn't count exactly how many damaged houses there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I think at a later stage, were you provided with photographs that had been taken at a later stage of the damage to Brisevo?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't think they were taken by you. Were they taken by somebody that you knew?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I did not myself take any of these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But having looked at them, are you able to confirm what they show and when the damage occurred?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes. I could recognise every single house and every single place that was photographed, because I lived there for almost 30 years.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And I'd like you, please, to have a look at the photographs in the order in which they are numbered, which starts with 0107-4759 onwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Your Honours, could they all be -- if Your Honours enter them into evidence, could they be made one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it's the understanding it should not be added to our famous binder, S15.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I think Ms. Sutherland would be very upset. I think it's better they stay with the witness as the witness's exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then it's -- I think there will be no objections by the Defence. Then, admitted into evidence as 185-1 and following.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Could we have the first photograph up which bears the number 4579.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What does that show us, Mr. Atlija?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: In this photograph, you can see the Catholic church in Brisevo. It was built in 1990.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're going to show a video later of what it looked like afterwards. Then please, the next photograph, 4760.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What does that show us?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: In this photograph, you can see the remains of Ante Mlinar's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was that one of the houses that was destroyed when you went through the village?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes. This house was burned down in the first onslaught, in a manner of speaking.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next photograph, 4761, what does that show us?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Here you can see the remains of, I think, Andjelko Mlinar's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, was that destroyed in that attack?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then next, 4762.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I think these are the remains of Ante Mlinar's house, but taken from a different angle.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the road that we can see here, is that the road that you indicated in the first drawing, or is that a different road?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: No, it's a different road. That's not the same as the one in the drawing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next, 4763.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: These are the remains of the Matic family house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's not easy to see, but I think we're going to see a close-up, are we not, in the next photograph? Yes, so if we can look at 4764. Is that the same house that we can see on the left of the previous photograph, but taken from a different angle?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I think so, but from a different angle.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think we can see clearly there the fire damage. Next, 4765, what are we looking at there?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: These are the remains of Stipo Dimac's house, but I think there's a better photograph where you can see the same thing better from a different angle.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, if we look at the last one, 4766. Is that the same house but at a different angle?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes. This is the same house. This is the photo I meant, a clearer view from a different angle.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And all these houses were damaged, were they, during that attack on your village?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I'm now going to ask for you to look at a video that you provided, which I believe the audiovisual unit have.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think the best way of dealing with this subject to Their Honours' consent is: It will be played, if there's anything that you want to explain, if you just say "stop" into the microphone, they'll pause the video. Okay, if we could --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not sure that's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the remains of the iron ore mine, Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Just pause for a moment, please. Just going to hold up.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When was that destroyed or attacked?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: There was no attack, strictly speaking, because no one was working there. They just targeted it and hit it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know when that was? Was that in the same period of time?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: That was around the same period of time, but it went on for several months. You couldn't do a thing like that in a very short time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I should have just done this before we go on. I think it's right, is it, this film was shot by a German cameraman, from a news station?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: ZDF, I think.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: ZDF, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Perhaps we can go back to it now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Still the iron ore mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think we can fast forward this a little bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If I think if you fast forward until we say stop or one of us says stop. Gripping there, the horses.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the very entrance to the mine, the gate from the direction of Ljubija. Stop, please. In this building, there were the offices of Slobodan and Djoko Karanjac, from the so-called Ljubija Serb command. I don't know what it's official name was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And this is where, in Ljubija itself, is it?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. We would like to go on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the town itself, Ljubija.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Pausing for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did anything happen to Ljubija? Was that in any way attacked?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Not while I was there. There were no attacks on Ljubija, no shelling, no military conflicts. But people were being taken off, maltreated, killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we go back, then, to the film, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And again, I think we can fast -- yes. All right, pause, please, there, what are we looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. Here, we can see the remains of that same Catholic church that we had seen in one of the previous photographs, the Catholic church in Brisevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was it in that state that we can see, and we will see a bit more of it in a moment, when you emerged that first day and had a look at the village?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes, precisely in that state.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. If we just have a look at it then, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you just pause the video there?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What are we looking at, although it may be obvious, Mr. Atlija.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: We could see the place in the church where the altar used to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. We could move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the interior of the church.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that is?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Here, you can see the rubble from the bell which hung in the belfry and then fell down at some point.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think we've seen sufficient. I'm not sure that the tracking equipment is doing terribly well. Thank you. Your Honour, I don't know when Your Honour is intending to have a second break, but I'm going to move on to the burial of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's appropriate to have the break now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. We resume at 5.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Atlija, I should have asked you, do you know when that video was taken from the cameraman from ZDF?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: The exact date, and the related data, I have all of that at home, but I can't give it to you now. I don't know these things by heart, so I'm afraid I might give you the wrong date.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If it becomes of importance, you can probably check for us when you get home.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, nonetheless, may I ask that that be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then admitted into evidence, S186.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just before I move on, may I confess to yet another sin, which is that I had forgotten that last year, Mr. Inayat took various photographs which are relevant to the evidence that Mr. Atlija is giving. He has never seen them. I have given copies to my learned friends. I think the best thing I can do, Your Honour, is I'm going to ask him if he's able to recognise things. If he's not, then they can't be admitted. And I will give Your Honours copies now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If this is your own sin, there's no problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There are probably worse ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Atlija, I want to come now to the subject of the bodies and the killings, starting with what you told us about the village. You told us that 68 people were killed during the course of this attack. Of those people, if there's no dispute about this, I'll lead the evidence rather than asking you to remember, were 14 women?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were two of them males who were under 16?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were there also four people killed who were invalids?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, you told us that the main bulk of the soldiers withdrew. Did they take with them any men in custody?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: 36 men were taken to, as we found out later, Krings, in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were those men all men between 18 and 65, in other words, of callup age?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I think they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And is it right that those men were released after two months, effectively through bribing somebody?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Nikola Marinovic was bribed. And it was through his intervention that all those people were released from the camp alive and not one of those people was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You told us that you witnessed yourself the killing of Pero Dimac. Did you witness the killings of the other persons, the other 68?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Only the killing of Pero Dimac personally. The other bodies, I only got to see when they were already dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I want to deal, please, with the burials that you participated in. Were the first people that you buried Pero Dimac and your father?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: They were the first, and we buried the same evening on the day they were killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We know where Pero was killed. Where did you find your father's body?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: We found my father's body about 15 or 20 metres further down from his house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were you able to see from his body what had caused his death?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: He had three gunshot wounds in his back.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And where did you bury your father?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: We buried him about 10 metres from the place where he was killed, because the soil was softer, and it was easier to dig there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, the following day, did you go through the village?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And whenever you found a dead body, would you bury the person that you found?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Not immediately, because soldiers would appear, and they would start shooting at us if they saw us there. So that we only managed to bury a number of bodies after three months.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And in addition to people who you found in the village, did you also - and I'm going to jump ahead, and then deal with each grave, as it were, separately - did you also find other people in other areas who had been killed?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: In two other places, yes, we did find other bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what I'm going to ask you about now, what you told the Croatian Information people about, namely, the various graves, did you either see the bodies, even if you weren't present at the actual burial or take part in the burial?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Some I only saw, but I did take part in most of the burials.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, then, I want to take these in the order that you dealt with them. The first grave that I want to ask you about, I think, was at the Stara Rijeka. I think it may assist, although I know you marked on a map the location of the various graves. It's not always the easiest to see. I think it's easier if you use the map that you drew the attacks on, because that I think shows most of the places.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I wonder if you could have back what is now our Exhibit S --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 184. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think the first grave that you gave information about was one in Stara Rijeka. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did there come a time shortly after the attack on Brisevo when a group of Muslims passed through your village or reached your village?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I did not see them myself, but other villagers told me that a group of about 12 Muslims indeed passed through our village and went off in the direction of Stari Majdan, for which they had to pass through Stara Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. And subsequently, did you, yourself, pass through when you were trying to go to Sanski Most, did you pass through Stara Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes, I did, a number of times.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you see any bodies there?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Across the way from Ljubica Dizdarevic's house, under a big pear tree, there was a heap of between 10 and 12 bodies. It was difficult to count them because they were covered over with earth, but hands and heads were sticking out of this little mound.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How close did you get to the bodies?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Very close, perhaps 5 or 6 metres, 10 at the most.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Those that you could see, their heads, what sort of age did they appear to be? Firstly, I'm sorry, what sex, first of all?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Those I could see were men.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you guess roughly what age these men were?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Young, I think, about 20 years of age. Not older.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you able to see in any of their cases what had caused their death?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Only on those bodies which were closer, there were blood stains which looked like bullet wounds.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And do you know yourself whether this grave was exhumed?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I think that only traces of excavation were found -- exhumation were found in that grave, not bodies actually. And they told me about this when they exhumed at a place called Jakerina Kos.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next I want to move to the hamlet we call Dimaci. Which if we look at your hand-drawn map, I think we can see to the right-hand side of Brisevo, I think it's not quite clear on the screen, but if you just point it out.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, was there a mass grave, in the sense of more than one person in it, there?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: In that grave, there were the remains of three bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know who they were?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Those were the bodies of Stipo Dimac, Franjo Marijan, and his wife, Mara Marijan.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know how old Stipo Dimac was, roughly?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Stipo Dimac was I think about 76 to 78 years old. I can't say with any precision.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you see the bodies?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I saw what remained of the bodies. The bodies were burned and were very difficult to identify.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And when you saw the bodies, were they inside a house or outside?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: The remains of the bodies were inside the house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And did you personally take part in the burial of those bodies?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: The burial itself, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think you, however, were present after the bodies were exhumed in September of 1998, and they were identified in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I was present also when the bodies were buried several days later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I should ask, how long after the attack on Brisevo did you see these bodies, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: At least three weeks. Maybe a day or two more.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know, and if you don't know, was this particular little hamlet or village attacked when the main attack took place on Brisevo?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: These are the fringe areas of the village, and they were attacked the first night of the attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Could we come to the hamlet of Mlinari. Mlinari. I think you're going to point out for us.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, how many people were buried there?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Many people were buried there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you see the bodies there?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I did see the bodies quite clearly because I took part in the burial.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What did you notice about those bodies?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Those bodies were also covered over with earth, but parts of the bodies were sticking out with wounds of irregular shapes, probably not inflicted by firearms. Next to the grave, there were some tools, a pick, a spade, which bore the stains -- bloodstains and hair.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you able to establish, from any eyewitnesses, what those people had been doing before they were killed?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: From the accounts of the eyewitnesses, they were made to dig their own grave, and then they were killed with the same tools they had used to dig the grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you, then, buried those people, did you, or reburied them?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes, we brought some more earth, and we buried the bodies in the hole that they were already lying in.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You've told us that they had irregular injuries, that they weren't shot. Could you tell from when you helped rebury them where their injuries were?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: During the exhumation, it was established, for instance, that Luka Mlinar had been killed with a pick on his head. And his skull was, in fact, fractured by the pick. However, there were also broken bones. What the cause of the death, well, I'm not a pathologist, a forensic expert, I cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Don't worry about that. Thank you. And you know that the grave was exhumed, but you weren't present -- you weren't present at the exhumation, but I think you were present at the reburial.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In addition to those bodies, were there any other bodies nearby?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: In the immediate vicinity, there was another grave where Joso Lovric had been killed, one of the four invalids I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you told us that there were many bodies in the -- at the main grave. Do you remember exactly how many?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: In the main grave there was Luka Mlinar, Ivica Mlinar, I think Jerko Ivandic was there, too, Milan Ivandic, and his two brothers. I cannot recall their names right now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I think one was called Pejo Ivandic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we move, then, please to the next place, which I think is the hamlet of Buzuci, which is -- you can see on the map.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Was there another grave there?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes. We buried people there also.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, how many -- how did you come across the bodies? Where were the bodies when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: If you are referring to the bodies in Buzuci, they were in a terrible shape. They were lying in front of Marko Buzuk's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And in what way were they in terrible shape?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Especially Milan Buzuk, he had cuts and wounds all over his body. And a part of his skull was missing, and we found him a few metres further. Ivica Buzuk was killed along with his crutch. He was wrapped up in his crutch, and we could not separate the body from the crutch.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you able to establish from anyone what had happened to Milan Buzuk?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: The mother of Milan Buzuk was an eyewitness, when he was caught, tortured, and killed. And she told me the story.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, do you know if that grave was later exhumed?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: The grave was exhumed at the same time as the others, in September 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then can we come, please, next to, I think, the hamlet of Jezerce. I'm not sure that's shown on the map, is it?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: You cannot see very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is it above Buzuci?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: It is, so to say, below Buzuci. The map isn't very accurate because it was drawn by hand. It is at a lower level than Buzuci.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't think, I'm afraid, any of the other maps will help us either. Again, did you find bodies there?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: There, we found bodies as well. Sreco Buzuk's body, Ivo Lovric's body, Vlatko Buzuk's body. He was also an invalid.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you able to establish how they died?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: There were bullet wounds, and in the underarms of Ivo Lovric, there was no skin. The skin was missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And again, I think those bodies were exhumed and they were reburied.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we move next please to the hamlet of Cengije, which I think is marked.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes, it is about there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. It's not marked actually, but it's marked on my copy. How many people there?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: There we found Marko Buzuk.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And when you found him, what sort of state was his body in?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: The lower part of his body was fully burned because even the grass and the weeds around him had been burnt as well. The upper part of his body was preserved, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And was this gentleman the father of Milan, the man you had described as being tortured?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then can we move next, please, to the hamlet of Mustanica. Just show us where that is.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: In the lower part of the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. And is that where Pero Dimac was buried?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes. Pero Dimac on one -- in one place, and my father Atlija was buried in another place.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And in fact, is there one other body in that area?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I cannot remember whether there was someone else buried in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you remember somebody called Ante Matanovic?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes, I remember Ante Matanovic. He was buried about 2 kilometres south from his house, but that part of that village is also called Mustanica, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's quite all right. Can you remember what sort of condition he was in when you found his body?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: He was also an invalid. And he was in a state as someone who had been running and was stopped abruptly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And could you ascertain from finding his body what had caused his death?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I think he was killed with a firearm. There was a bullet wound.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And you say it looked as though he was running away and he was stopped. Was the bullet wound in the front or the back, can you remember?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I think on the back.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Now, was one person buried near the church?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Near the church, Jozo Jakara was buried.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you see his body?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes, we saw his body.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And were you able to ascertain, or if not you personally, somebody, how he had died?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I didn't come near him really, but those that did said that his throat had been slit with glass.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, next, can we deal with a hamlet called Ivandici, if you can just point that out on the map.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Here, but it hasn't been marked on the map. That hamlet has not been indicated on the map, at least on the map that I have before me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just thinking, in fact, for the purposes of the transcript, I suppose one ought to say that the witness indicated just near the letter K in Kurevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, there were a number of graves -- are there a number of graves located in that hamlet?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: There were several graves, but they were close to one another. And then we marked them as one grave. I think that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, how many people were there?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Several people, practically the whole Ivandic family, Stipo, his wife, his two sons -- I don't know their names any more.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And roughly how many women, can you remember? You said there was --

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: In that place, there were three or four women.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, how did you find the bodies?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: When we were visiting the village, we passed by that location, and we spoke with the other survivors. And everyone who knew that someone -- that there was a body or a grave, he spoke to us, and then we visited the entire area.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The bodies, were you able to see what had caused their death?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Not in the case of all of them. But with most of them, we could see bullet wounds.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, again, going back to the hamlet of Cengije, is there another mass grave there, other than the one you've already described?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: There was. In that area, there was also another grave in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us about the grave which was close to somebody called Ivo Zunic's house.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: The grave near Ivo Zunic's house was similar to the one that we described. There were several people killed and buried very close to one another. So it can be considered as one grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were there any women in that grave, or graves?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I think there were women in -- that there were women in that grave, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And in particular, was there somebody called Kaja Komljen?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Kaja Komljen was found in a field. Her body was totally naked, and there were many wounds on her body. But we didn't notice any bullet wounds.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you able to discover from any witnesses what had happened to her?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: The eyewitnesses, including her brother, said that she had been raped and beaten until she died.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The other people in the grave, in those collection of small graves, were you able to establish how they had died?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Most of bullet wounds, but the eyewitness said that Luka Komljen and his son Iva had been tortured for hours before they were killed, but I wasn't an eyewitness to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Again, I think the bodies have been exhumed from that grave as well.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: All the bodies were exhumed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And can we deal, please, with graves on the Raljas hill, which I think you have marked on the map.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I marked this on the map. We can see the top of the hill, and the grave is actually a bit further down the slope.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think that there were two graves, were there not?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Two individual graves. I think there is the 14-year-old Luka Mlinar buried in one of them, and in the other, the 14- or 15-year-old boy called Mirsad Svraka. And he was not from our village. He was from Rizvanovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then again, I think one further grave in the hamlet of Mlinari. Was that for a 74 year old woman called Mara Mlinar?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes, Mara Mlinar was buried there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you see her body?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I did, but I didn't come very close.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Where was her body when you saw it?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: It was in a field. Those who buried her said that she had been killed by the shrapnel of the mortar.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I want to come now, to the Redak graves or killings. Can you tell us where Redak is? I'm not sure you've marked it.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Redak is where two paths fork from the Ljubija road. One in the direction of Gornja Ravska, and one in the direction of Brisevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. When did you first come across the bodies?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Just after the attack on Brisevo, a friend of mine and I tried to pass through to Gornja Ravska, and that's when we saw this heap of bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Whereabouts were the bodies?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: The bodies were in a place where a path forks off for Brisevo for the Ljubija Stara Rijeka road. There is a hole there, partly filled with water, and close by, there are several dumper tyres. And that's how the place could be identified.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'd just like you for a moment, please, to have a look at this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. photograph, which you haven't been shown before.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Your Honours, if he can identify it, I'll just hand it out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that the place?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes, I think this is the place.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, these photographs were taken last year by Mr. Inayat. Can I hand out copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Is it correct that we saw this picture already beforehand?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You've seen it already, have you? Right. Your Honour, I'm told rightly that Your Honour may have seen it with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Mr. Karagic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour is quite right. And Ms. Karper has told me the same thing. So in that case, I needn't re-exhibit it. It's been exhibited, has it? Only Ms. Karper doesn't see it on her screen. Your Honour, I think a check is being made to see whether it has been exhibited. But we can move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before you found these bodies, had you heard about these killings?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I had heard that buses with Muslims from the surrounding villages of Prijedor were taken through Ljubija and being taken to Redak, and that the buses were returned to Ljubija empty.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Had anybody come to your village and told you what had happened?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: As far as those who were killed at Redak, we did not know what had happened until a boy about 16, 17 years of age came running all frightened, telling us that he had fled from one of these executions. But the conversation only lasted several seconds, and then we fled in a different direction. We didn't ask him for his name or any other personal data.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was that the first time you'd seen that boy before?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: It was the first time I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Have you seen him again recently?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: The young man at a hotel greeted me, said "thanks" and that his name was Nermin Karagic and that he was the boy that he had met then, there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The bodies that you saw, can you remember roughly how many people there were?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Quite many. We thought even as many as 200.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you, yourselves, bury these bodies?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: No, we just had a look, and then we ran off and never approached the place again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we've decided that this photograph appears on one of the maps. I don't know whether it has been formally exhibited yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I just have a look, but I think we saw also in connection with this other map not only the small pictures around the map, but separately these pictures. But indeed, I can't identify an S number.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, just so that everybody knows what he looked at, for the purpose of the transcript at the moment can I just read out the ERN number on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. And let's give these photos provisional, the next following dash I believe 7, number 185 to the other photos linked to the witness before us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. And the ERN number shown on this is 02033348.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, finally -- Your Honour wanted to deal with other matters?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: On the graves, did you find a grave in the Kurevo hills?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I couldn't exactly call that a grave. We found piles of bodies, so to speak. They were not exactly buried in a grave or anything resembling a grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you remember roughly when you saw these bodies?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: This may have been in August. We were trying to reach Ljubija and Sanski Most, and we moved a lot about that particular area.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you know who those bodies were? I mean, the actual names, but where they came from?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: We are convinced that those were people from the surrounding Muslim villages who tried to run to Stari Majdan or to a different place, Hambarine, Carakovo, Rizvanovici, Biscani, Zecovi.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And how were you able to -- What convinces you of that?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Later on, other eyewitnesses passed by and told us about it. But we witnessed ourselves when the soldiers set up ambushes along a road above the Kurevo Road. They brought a praga and Bofors, and we heard when they started firing at the forest. We heard yells and screams, people running. These who escaped whom we sometimes met later on, they said they were from Carakovo, Rizvanovici, Biscani, and that many of them had been killed and remained there in the forest.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, finally, on the question of these graves and exhumations, you've told us you were present at the reburials. Were a number of people reburied in a cemetery in Brisevo?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: The cemetery is called Raljas and is on Raljas hill, the hill that we've spoken about. Part of the bodies were transferred to Croatia and buried there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. I want you to have a look, please, then at a photograph of -- perhaps you can just identify two photographs, in fact. And then I'll hand Your Honours copies. Does that show the first --

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: This is not difficult to identify. This is the Raljas grave.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then if you look at the next photograph, please, does that show your father?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: Yes. This is the grave slab with my father's name. He's buried in that grave alongside with other persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Your Honours, I don't think Your Honours have had these photographs before, have you? Can I hand out copies again and ask they be exhibited as additional ones. I think it would be 9 and 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 10 and 11 now. There are no objections; therefore, admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And just the ERN numbers of those for the transcript are, for the large grave, photograph 02033351; and the close-up, 02033352. The Defence have got it. Thank you. I'll have them back, thank you. That's our only set. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, just while we're on the subject of photographs, I want you to look at this one, please, which is particularly awful, but let's see if we can get some assistance.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think maybe Your Honours will need to have copies in front of you, because it is a particularly terrible photograph.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are you able to recognise that?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: It's quite difficult, but I think I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What are we looking at in that photograph? If you can't recognise anything, say so.

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: No problem. I think these are the remains of the shop and the school building, and up here the remains of the church. But I must say this again: I'm not positive about this, because the image is not very clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. If that is the church --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Your Honour we can confirm it through Mr. Inayat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you just explain to us by looking at this photograph, when the attack came, where were the -- we've seen it on your map. Where were the troops based?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: To the south where the 6th Krajina Brigade came from, that's where the picture was taken from, the bottom of the photograph, there is a path, a road, across a plain. Around the village, all the way to the church. From this side of the road, on this side of the road and all the way around, there were soldiers. And on these hills from Ljubija was the 5th Kozara Brigade. And here, the 6th Krajina Brigade from where they descended to the centre of the village here in the valley, and then returned toward the church. And here is the Dizdari elevation, which we have also referred to, where they eventually dispersed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, subject to confirmation, and I don't think I'm anticipating too much by saying it will be confirmed by Mr. Inayat that is the church, may that be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The witness has explained a lot on this picture. No objections. Therefore, admitted into evidence as S185-12, which is an enlargement of picture number 4 on S169.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the number is 02033350.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think finally this afternoon, has anybody gone back to live in Brisevo?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: No one, as far as I know, returned to live there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Have any of the, to your knowledge, any of the houses, anything like that, been rebuilt?

utterances.speaker: IVO ATLIJA
utterances.text: I know that one man, Andjelko Mlinar, did build a house there, but he doesn't live there. So it's only one house we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. I haven't quite finished the evidence, but Your Honours I have only got another half hour tomorrow, I think. I think I ought to say I think we're going to have a problem over witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: First of all, I have to thank you for your informations of today. And we'll hear your additional evidence tomorrow afternoon. And you're excused for today. We will proceed for another five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we either seem to underestimate or overestimate. This was thought this witness would take Thursday and Friday, and I certainly, as I say, won't be more than half an hour tomorrow morning. And I'm told that cross-examination is not likely to be that long. The next witness is only due to arrive on Sunday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Probably there is a possibility, then, to hear Mr. Inayat. I think it will take a long time to hear this witness, especially in cross-examination, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's what occurred to us, that we could recall Mr. Inayat to testify to fill in the time. I see Mr. Ostojic --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If that's the only option that we have, Your Honour, but I actually had made arrangements for Friday that are of a personal nature. So I would -- I was not going to be in attendance before the Court in this case. But we'll proceed accordingly, however the wishes to proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Probably there might be another investigator to be heard immediately, a person who is available in this premises for Friday, or probably starting on Thursday?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not quite clear what Your Honour is referring to, but I'll make inquires of Mr. Koumjian. There's another --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: There are, I believe, two other investigators on the list from the premises. And we should come back to this issue tomorrow. Unfortunately, we can then only decide tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll certainly make inquiries of Mr. Koumjian as to who is available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. But let's immediately, then, first of all I would like to invite the OTP to give their response on the motion under Rule 95, the new one of July 3, 2002, no later than Monday next week. Will this be feasible?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I thought Your Honour was going to say right now. As I hadn't read it, it was going to be difficult. Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it should be carefully dealt with. And no doubt, as regards the other motion to exclude the prior motion, no doubt, it's granted as requested, thereby the former motion is declared moot and the Trial Chamber is no longer seized with this other first motion. We still have to come back to this from today. Then finally, we can maybe hear the observations as regards the request for subpoena.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. And before I address the issue of the subpoena, if I may, I'm not sure if I misunderstood the Court, our motion that was filed is not pursuant to Rule 95. We withdrew that motion, just so that the record is clear on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, with respect to the request for subpoena by the OTP, we feel, in essence, that it fails to establish the necessary prerequisites in order to mandate that such an order be issued by the Court. Namely, we feel the subpoena is overbroad and overreaching in the following respects: Their request under paragraph number 1 clearly asks for items which constitute privileged materials. They conveniently exclude, and we thank them for that, the attorney/client privilege, however there are other privileges that are incorporated in the request for items that they seek. On paragraph number 1 (i) as it's identified in their request, they ask for medical records, they ask for letters signed or handwritten by Dr. Milomir Stakic, which would include materials that he wrote to and from his wife, presumably. Also, to and from any pastoral privileges that may exist, because I'm aware of one such letter which we believe constitutes a privilege that he should not give to the Court or to the OTP. The basis, however, of our request or the foundation of the Prosecutor's request, can be found on page 2 of their supporting affidavit or declaration. In there, they only set forth, as the minimum criteria, that the request they are seeking would be helpful. They do not set the proper foundation, which we believe is necessary under the rules, both Rule 54 and 39, which would be a request to say that they have exhausted all other remedies, that they have, in fact, requiring the material because it is critical and necessary for any purpose within their case. The Defence, however, does not object to the request made on paragraph 2 of their request which includes documents such as, but we think it should be limited to, driver's license, passport, and any materials that Dr. Stakic, when he was incarcerated, had on his possession at that time. In addition, the Defence does not object to any signatures that were required of Dr. Stakic, during the initial appearance and initial processing during the incarceration. However, we strongly feel that the request is overbroad in asking for letters and other documents. By way of an example of the breadth of their request, they are seeking, in essence, all materials that Dr. Stakic is currently drafting during the proceedings of this trial, meaning notes, his own impressions of witnesses and/or items that are occurring within and throughout the trial. We have not found one case or one decisional authority in the Tribunal which would allow such an overreaching and overbroad subpoena as the one requested here. In fact, the decisional authority in this Tribunal has been, thus far, at the very least, to prohibit testing or requesting that an accused give handwriting samples. We think this request is actually an attempt to circumvent that current prevailing decisional authority. And so we would ask that either the subpoena be withdrawn and the request be modified, or that the Court, because the subpoena is overbroad within its own powers, restructure it to limit it to the provisions under paragraph 1 (ii) of their request. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Any observations in return?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, the defendant, the accused, I'm sorry, has refused to provide us with handwriting samples. The accused, for the very first time, raised an issue over handwriting when this trial began. It has never, ever been an issue raised in the pretrial brief or at any hearing before this trial began. Your Honours have ordered the Prosecution to obtain a graphologist, an expert, to examine the disputed handwritings and give Your Honours the benefit of an expert opinion. In order to do that, we can only do that if we can provide an expert, it's common sense, general knowledge, it doesn't need somebody to say that, of specific samples of the admitted handwriting of the person who has himself raised the issue that this handwriting is not his. The summons is a perfectly proper summons. It is not an attempt to circumvent any decision of this Court. That decision, which in our submission in any event, is wrongly decided, simply says that a defendant cannot be compelled to testify against himself. Fine. But we, the OTP, have the power to request Your Honours, and Your Honours have the power to grant us, to obtain handwriting samples without which Your Honours will not have the benefit of at least trying to see where the truth in this case lies, which is what Your Honours are mandated to do. Your Honours, we have specifically excluded any privileged documents, letters to Mr. Stakic's -- Dr. Stakic's wife are not privileged. It is well known that any of these communications, which are in the Detention Unit, are not privileged documents other than that between client and lawyer. Your Honour, we invite Your Honour to grant the summons as drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm confident the Court has reviewed the decisional authority in question, examine it does not say that you only have a right to remain silent or cannot be compelled to testify. The case law clearly says the Court cannot -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You refer to Mutic, then we can cut the story short. The Mutic decision of January 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think it's Delic, Your Honour, in the Celebici case, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, we speak about the same case. We are aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just to add as a comment, I think it is a privilege that the client has, that all of us have, in keeping what is considered our own impressions of the trial that's going on. What would happen if this Court set a precedent that said at the end of the case for the defendant, we're going to compel the defendants or the accused to turn in all the notes that they have taken throughout the trial so that the OTP can, during their rebuttal case, enjoy the benefit of all the comments, whether they are positive or negative as it may relate to both the OTP, the Defence lawyers, presumably even the Court, much less the witnesses, which are critical. I think it's clearly overbroad. We do not have an objection, as I said, and I must reiterate it, to paragraph 1 (ii), which would be the materials and the passport and in the signatures that he has provided. I just have to add one comment, because I cannot allow this statement to be made: The burden of proof is not on us. The OTP continuously insists that we are making denials. They have the burden of proof. They have the burden of proof to establish the element both as to authenticity, foundation, on each and every element. I know it's convenient for them to continuously shift that to us; we continue to resist that. And we're resisting it because it's a matter of right and it's a fundamental right guaranteed to us by the rules of this Tribunal. And we are exercising those rights, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think both opinions have been made quite clear. They are exchanged, and they form the basis for the decision of this Trial Chamber which will be handed down as soon as possible. The trial stands adjourned until tomorrow, 2.15.
